title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on How to Apply Article 13 of the Land Administration Law and Article 14 of the Forest Law

articles.content_en: 1. Article 13 of the Land Administration Law and Article 14 of the Forest Law provide that disputes over ownership and use right of land, trees, and forestland between parties shall be handled by the people's government at or above the county level; if a party is not satisfied with the ruling of the people's government, it may file a prosecution with the People's Court. Although such cases have been handled by the people's government, their nature remains civil rights and interests disputes; when adjudicating such cases, the People's Court shall still take the original disputing parties as the parties to the litigation.

2. According to the provisions of Article 13, paragraph 5 of the Land Administration Law and Article 14, paragraph 4 of the Forest Law, prior to the resolution of disputes over ownership and use right of land, trees, and forestland, neither party shall change the current state of the land, shall not fell the disputed trees, and shall not damage the attachments on the land. Therefore, after the people's government makes a ruling, if any party files a prosecution with the People's Court, during the period of adjudication by the People's Court, the subject matter in dispute shall be maintained in its original state, and the attribution of ownership or use right shall ultimately be determined by the ruling of the People's Court.

3. Where such cases are brought to the People's Court according to law, they shall be accepted by the Civil Adjudication Tribunal.
This is a reply.
31 July 1987
